title: Async writeback latency leak — detection, mitigations, and rollback plan
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
A production incident on 2026-02-07 caused sustained eviction storms and memory growth on a subset of prefix cache shards serving multi-tenant workloads. Root cause analysis points to a slow async writeback path that caused writeback queues to grow and interleave with eviction decisions, resulting in stale index entries, delayed reclaim, and cascading prefetched hot-entries that amplified memory usage.

Impact:
- Affected 6% of serving nodes in us-west-2 for ~3.5 hours before automated backpressure limited incoming prefetched writes.
- Increased p99 tail latency for generation requests by ~220ms on impacted nodes and forced global fallbacks for several high-throughput tenants.
- Elevated memory allocation leading to OOM restarts for two pods and degraded throughput for 12 customer-facing endpoints.

Timeline (brief):
- 2026-02-07 02:12 UTC: On-call alert for eviction-rate surge and persistent high memory usage.
- 2026-02-07 02:30 UTC: Traffic routing to fallback model variants enabled; mitigations reduced customer impact.
- 2026-02-07 05:40 UTC: Service returned to stable memory profile after adaptive backpressure and manual eviction of prefetched namespaces.

Root cause (summary):
- Async writeback worker retries for some tenant namespaces encountered transient kernel scheduling delays causing writeback latency to balloon.
- The eviction scoring component relied on up-to-date writeback acknowledgements; delayed acks produced stale occupancy estimates and prevented timely reclaim.
- Prefetch subsystem continued to insert entries for hot prefixes while writeback backlog persisted, amplifying memory growth (reentrant prefetch).
- Lack of a fast-path drain/backoff for writeback queue meant backpressure was only applied at very high queue sizes, too late for some tenants.

Reproduction steps (local / load test):
1. Configure kvcache with heavy prefetched workload over 16 namespaces and force an artificial writeback latency (simulate with sleep() in writeback thread).
2. Drive sustained requests that trigger prefetch in 8 namespaces concurrently.
3. Observe writeback queue growth, eviction score staleness, and p99 latency increase.

Telemetry findings / artifacts:
- Grafana dashboard (runbook incident panel): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv_incident/async-writeback-2026-02
- Heap profiles and heap growth trace: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/kv/heap/2026-02-07.zip
- Correlated GHPR for emergency rollback (links in comments).

Immediate mitigations applied (during incident):
- Enabled conservative prefetch backoff (prefetch_rate_limit -> 0.25) for all tenants on affected nodes.
- Triggered a manual compaction and aggressive eviction for prefetched namespaces on impacted nodes.
- Adjusted routing to shift ~40% traffic away from affected hosts.

Planned short-term fixes (next 2 weeks):
- Add a bounded writeback queue and an exponential backoff that rejects new prefetch inserts once queue > threshold (owner: Evan).
- Fast-path eviction trigger when writeback-ack-lag > 500ms to prioritize reclaiming space irrespective of stale scores (owner: Priya Desai).
- Add a synthetic tracer to writeback worker to emit per-tenant latency histograms and queue-depth alerts (owner: Daniel Park).

Planned long-term changes (3+ weeks):
- Rework eviction scoring to decouple from synchronous writeback acknowledgements; compute occupancy using amortized dwell-time heuristics and conservative defaults when writeback metrics are stale (owner: SRE team / runtime).
- Add tenant-scoped writeback quotas and isolation: prevent a misbehaving tenant from monopolizing writeback bandwidth and memory (owner: Platform).
- Introduce prefetch admission control that uses global memory budget and per-tenant budgets to avoid reentrant prefetch cascades (owner: Prefetch team).

Acceptance criteria / definition of done:
- No coordinated eviction storms in synthetic stress tests with induced writeback latency (runbook automation).
- New writeback-queue-backed alarms firing at simulated thresholds with clear runbook steps.
- Observability: per-tenant writeback latency charts are populated and appear in Console runtime-1.20 dashboard.

Rollout plan:
1. Merge bounded-queue + backoff change behind feature flag; enable on canary pool (5% of serving nodes).
2. Run 72h of soak with synthetic writeback-latency tests.
3. Gradual rollout by capacity (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with SLO guardrails; automated rollback on error budget breach.

Rollback plan:
- If regressions observed, toggle feature flag off and trigger immediate eviction sweep to reclaim prefetched entries, then re-evaluate thresholds.

Owner / Contacts:
- Incident owner: Evan Stone (assignee)
- Primary SRE: Priya Desai
- Prefetch lead: Daniel Park
- Runtime lead: Miguel Alvarez

Next steps (short):
- [ ] Draft PR for bounded writeback queue (ENG-101778 referenced in comments).
- [ ] Add runbook entries and update Console dashboard panels.
- [ ] Schedule follow-up postmortem review with SRE, Runtime, and Prefetch teams on 2026-03-12.
